direction: Diversity-first population search in a different basin, with hard time discipline: generate $8$--$16$ independent random codes and optimise them in a batched numpy Adam quench on the smooth energy $\sum_{i<j}\exp((\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-m)/T)$ with $T$ annealed $0.03\to0.002$ over $\sim3000$ vectorised steps (all replicas stacked in one array so this takes seconds, not minutes), then rank survivors not by score alone but by contact-graph fingerprint (sorted degree sequence at tol $10^{-6}$ plus the sorted Gram spectrum), discarding any replica whose fingerprint is within a small distance of the record's $20$--$39$-versus-$0$--$19$ split. LP-polish only the best two genuinely distinct survivors for $\le20$s each, cross them by taking the 39 lowest-personal-max points from each (after orthogonal Procrustes alignment) and re-polishing, and cap `solve()` at $160$s total with the incumbent returned from a checkpoint variable so a timeout can never destroy the result.

idea: Rigidly rotate one cluster against the other to change all cross cosines at once while preserving intra-cluster cosines, optimizing 6 plane angles on cross max then LP polishing.
direction: Collective rotation of the two visible clusters relative to each other: split the code into cluster A (indices $0$--$56$, equivalently PC1 $<-0.05$) and cluster B (the rest), compute orthonormal bases $U_A,U_B$ for their spans and the principal angles between them, then parametrise a relative rotation of all of B by a skew-symmetric generator supported only on cross directions, $X_B(\Theta)=X_B\exp(\Theta)$ with $\Theta$ built from the top $3$--$6$ principal vector pairs plus $2$--$4$ random cross pairs (angles in $[-0.35,0.35]$). Because this preserves every intra-B cosine exactly while changing all A--B cosines at once, optimise these few angles directly on the true max cosine (Nelder--Mead or CMA-ES, a few hundred evaluations, each just a $78\times78$ Gram update), interleave one short LP polish per accepted rotation, and alternate with the symmetric move rotating A instead. This is a move no per-point perturbation can imitate and directly attacks the unmixed two-block structure.

idea: Dual-stress-guided topology surgery using HiGHS marginals to release blocking pairs and step high-stress points along floppy modes of the weighted tangent rigidity matrix.
direction: Dual-stress-guided topology surgery, not displacement kicks: run the existing LP polish once, extract the HiGHS dual marginals on the tight pairs (slack $<10^{-8}$) as contact stresses, and build the weighted tangent rigidity matrix $R=\sum_{(i,j)\,\mathrm{tight}} w_{ij}\,(\text{tangent gradients})(\text{tangent gradients})^\top$; delete/release the $10$--$30$ tight pairs whose dual stress is zero or negative (they block motion without supporting the optimum), identify the $5$--$15$ points with the largest total stress, and take a coordinated step for exactly those points along the lowest eigenvectors of $R$ (step sizes $0.01,0.03,0.1$ in both signs, chosen by true max-cosine after renormalisation), then re-polish with the LP restricted to the surviving contact set. Loop over a few stress recomputations under a strict $150$s internal deadline, always returning the best checkpoint; success criterion is a changed sorted contact-degree sequence, not merely a smaller LP residual.

Excise a connected high-degree core cluster using near-contact graph and greedily reinsert many points into voids followed by Adam quench and selective LP polish.
direction: Core excision with coordinated multi-point reinsertion, not rattler moves: using near-contacts at tolerance $10^{-4}$--$10^{-3}$ (not $10^{-9}$), score points by contact degree and personal max, delete a connected cluster of $10$--$14$ highest-degree core points (plus their most-shared neighbours), then sequentially reinsert them from $8192$ random unit candidates by greedily minimising the maximum dot against the kept points and already-reinserted points; jitter the kept core by $0.005$--$0.015$ to break exact ties, run a cheap tangent-Adam log-sum-exp quench ($\beta:50\to400$, $\sim600$ steps), and only LP-polish candidates whose smooth max is below $\sim0.175$, with a hard internal deadline of $150$s and immediate return of the incumbent if nothing beats it. Repeat for several seeds/cluster choices, accepting by post-polish max first and by reduced near-contact count at $t-10^{-4}$ second, because success requires deleting $\sim100$ core contacts simultaneously rather than relocating free points.

idea: Batched isotropic multi-start with annealed log-sum-exp plus tangent Adam and covariance/variance penalties to find a balanced basin, then LP-polish distinct replicas.
direction: Batched fresh multi-start search for a balanced basin, ignoring the record except as fallback: simulate $32$ independent random codes simultaneously with batched Gram matrices, tangent Adam on annealed log-sum-exp ($\beta:20\to300$, $\sim1000$ steps) plus explicit penalties $\lambda_1\lVert X^\top X/78-I_{15}/15\rVert_F^2$ and $\lambda_2\,\mathrm{Var}_i(\max_{j\ne i}\langle x_i,x_j\rangle)$ to enforce isotropy and equal personal maxima, then cluster the replicas by max cosine, covariance eigen-spread, contact-degree variance, and sorted top-$200$ pair cosines; discard near-duplicates of the record fingerprint, LP-polish only the best $2$--$3$ genuinely distinct replicas for $\le15$s each under a $160$s total cap. This directly searches for the homogeneous tight-frame-like structure the incumbent lacks instead of perturbing around its two-strata topology.

Dual-weighted contact-exemption surgery that forces the largest-dual jammed-core pairs below threshold with a hinge penalty while minimizing the rest, then restores the full objective to land in a new contact topology.
direction: Dual-guided contact-exemption surgery to change the active topology: solve the current LP once, extract HiGHS dual marginals for active pairs, and select $30$--$80$ pairs with largest dual weight concentrated in the jammed core; for several rounds optimise a modified objective in which those pairs are exempt from the minimised threshold $t$ but receive a hinge penalty pushing their cosines below $m-0.002$--$m-0.005$, while all non-exempt pairs are minimised by log-sum-exp or by an LP with the exempt rows removed, then restore the full objective and LP-polish. Cycle through different exempt sets (largest-dual, highest-common-neighbour, random core edges) for short $5$--$10$s attempts each, keeping a candidate only if its restored local optimum differs in contact-graph fingerprint (sorted pair-cosines/contact degrees) from the record basin, even if an intermediate stage is worse.

idea: 6x13 cyclic-orbit ansatz with vectorized seed gradients on rising log-sum-exp then symmetry-breaking release and LP polish, falling back to incumbent if orbit basin is unpromising.
direction: Exact $6\times13$ cyclic-orbit ansatz followed by symmetry-breaking release: construct $78=6\cdot13$ points from six seed vectors in $\mathbb R^{15}$ by applying the $13$ cyclic permutations to the first $13$ coordinates while keeping the last two coordinates fixed within each orbit, giving exactly $78$ points with equal personal maxima and contact degrees inside every orbit by construction; optimise only the six seeds ($90$ parameters, with a precomputed permutation index array and either scatter-add analytic gradients or L-BFGS-B numerical gradients) on log-sum-exp at rising $\beta=100\to800$, avoiding periodic seeds that would duplicate points, then unfold to all $78$ points, add tiny $10^{-3}$ symmetry-breaking noise, and finish with the trust-region LP under a strict time cap. If an orbit code reaches even $\sim0.18$ before release, its balanced topology makes it a promising new basin; if not, return the incumbent unchanged well before the limit.

idea: Escape the layered jammed basin with isotropic whitening, sign-flip/block mixing and hole reinsertion diversified quenches screened by fast soft-max repulsion, then single trust-region LP squeeze.
Rebalance the dense/sparse PC1 strata by moving boundary points to alternative allocations and optimizing only stratum levels plus a relative rotation before release.
direction: Explicitly rebalance the two strata instead of perturbing individual points: rotate the record into its PCA basis, cluster the first-principal-coordinate values into the apparent dense/sparse strata (about $58/20$), and enumerate alternative allocations such as $65/13$, $61/17$, $55/23$, $52/26$, and $49/29$ by moving boundary points between strata while initially preserving all coordinates orthogonal to PC1 and rescaling each moved point to unit length. For each allocation, first optimise only a low-dimensional model consisting of the two stratum PC1 levels, one relative orthogonal rotation generated by a skew-symmetric matrix in the leading $6\times6$ PCA block, and tangential Adam steps for the moved points, using log-sum-exp with $\beta=100,300,900$ and at most 8 seconds per allocation; only candidates whose true maximum falls below $0.175$ before release should receive full-vector L-BFGS smoothing, and only candidates below the incumbent should receive a capped 15-second LP polish. Keep a strict internal deadline of 160 seconds and always return the best fully evaluated configuration, because stratum-size change is a discrete topology change that ordinary basin hopping has not tested.

idea: Build fresh isotropic basins from rotated-basis unions and whitened Gaussian seeds, then quench with annealed Adam on LSE repulsion plus centroid/tight-frame penalties before releasing penalties and LP-snapping.

idea: Core-targeted topology hops with isotropising kicks and fast annealed tangential Adam quench plus selective LP snap.

After all insertions, run alternating cycles of single-point best-hole relocation for points participating in the current maximum and joint L-BFGS smoothing, reserving the final 20 seconds for LP polishing; this directly destroys hundreds of simultaneous active constraints rather than trying to move against them.
